title.rendered: 50 Engaging IB CAS Project Ideas For IB Diploma Students

content.rendered:
IB CAS ideas (Creativity, Activity, Service) is a crucial component of the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP), providing students with the opportunity to engage in experiential learning outside the classroom. Through a range of diverse and exciting activities, students are encouraged to develop new skills, broaden their perspectives, and contribute positively to their community. 

In this blog, we will explore some of the best IB CAS activity ideas for students and how they can benefit from engaging in these activities. From creative pursuits to physical challenges, and community service initiatives, we will showcase the many ways in which IB CAS can help students grow and thrive.

Furthermore, Ignite Training Institute offers full educational support for the IB curriculum. Contact our expert consultants for more information.

50 Fun IB CAS Project Ideas For IB Diploma Students 

IB CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service) remains a core part of the International Baccalaureate(IB) program, fostering well-rounded students through creative exploration, physical activities, and community service. With evolving global challenges and digital innovations, CAS projects now offer even broader opportunities for meaningful impact.

Here are 50 of the most current and rewarding CAS project ideas to help you thrive:

Creativity-Based CAS Project Ideas

1. Launch A Podcast Or Vlog

Start a school or community podcast/video series discussing student life, mental health, sustainability, or any topic you love.

2. Learn A Dance Style & Perform

Master a new dance form like K-pop, salsa, or hip hop and choreograph a performance for school events.

3. Curate A Personal Art Exhibition

Showcase your artwork or invite peers to contribute. Host it physically or online for wider reach.

4. Start A Student Theatre Club

Write, direct, and perform short plays or skits addressing student concerns or global topics.

5. Film A Short Documentary 

Pick a meaningful community issue and document it. Share your video to raise awareness.

6. Create a Graphic Novel or Comic Series 

Illustrate stories addressing social issues or student life. Publish digitally or print copies for school.

7. Start A Dance Or Music Club 

Gather friends passionate about music or dance and hold regular performances or workshops.

8. Upcycle And DIY Projects Club 

Organize workshops teaching creative upcycling techniques using waste materials.

9. Design Sustainable Jewelry 

Make eco-friendly jewelry and host a fundraising sale for charity.

10. Master Calligraphy & Teach Workshops 

Learn calligraphy and offer classes to younger students or community members. This activity sharpens fine motor skills while promoting artistic expression and community engagement.

11. Develop A School Zone Or Newsletter 

Collaborate with peers to publish monthly news, creative writing, interviews, and student artwork. It builds writing, editing, and teamwork skills while keeping the school community informed and connected.

12. Create An Online Art Gallery

Collect digital submissions from students and curate an online exhibition to celebrate creative talent. This fosters appreciation for the arts and gives students a platform to showcase their work to a wider audience.

13. Organize A Cultural Food Festival

Bring the school community together by sharing recipes, traditions, and dishes from diverse backgrounds. It promotes multicultural understanding and creates a fun, collaborative atmosphere.

14. Host A Photography Competition 

Focus on themes like “My City”, “Climate Change”, or “Hidden Stories” to engage creativity. This project encourages artistic thinking while raising awareness on important social and environmental issues.

15. Design Posters For School Campaigns 

Help the school’s environment, mental health, or kindness drives by creating promotional materials.

Activity-Based CAS Project Ideas

16. Organize A Charity Run Or Walkathon

Combine fitness with fundraising by planning a local event for a cause that matters to you.

17. Lead Weekly Fitness Sessions 

Host morning yoga, zumba, or HIIT classes for classmates or teachers.

18. Train For A Challenge Event

Pick a personal goal like a marathon, triathlon, or a long-distance cycling trip, and document your progress.

19. Start A Beginner’s Sports Club

Organize casual games in soccer, volleyball, or basketball to encourage new players.

20. Lead A Hiking Or Nature Exploration Group

Organize regular hikes and share knowledge about local wildlife and environmental conservation.

21. Plan A Weekend Yoga Retreat

Spend time improving physical and mental wellbeing through yoga and meditation workshops.

22. Organize Self-Defense Classes

Learn martial arts or self-defense and host training sessions for peers or younger students.

23. Create An Online Fitness Blog Or App

Share workout routines, fitness challenges, and health advice with your school community.

24. Host Dance Marathon Fundraisers 

Dance non-stop for charity! Challenge your school to participate in this fun, active event.

25. Lead A Park Or Beach Fitness Clean-Up Day 

Mix physical activity with service by organizing a community clean-up.

Service-Based CAS Project Ideas

26. Organize Weekly Tutoring For Younger Students

Support academic growth by mentoring or tutoring students in subjects you excel in.

27. Start A Community Garden Project

Transform an empty space into a garden, teaching sustainability and growing fresh produce.

28. Volunteer At Animal Shelters

Spend time caring for shelter animals and help with adoption awareness campaigns.

29. Lead An Environmental Awareness Campaign

Host workshops and create social media content promoting sustainability and climate action.

30. Plan A School-Wide Food Drive

Collect non-perishable items for local food banks or charities. This project raises awareness about hunger and encourages student participation in supporting the community.

31. Organize A Blood Donation Drive

Partner with local organizations to host a blood donation camp at your school. It helps save lives and educates students about the importance of blood donations.

32. Launch A Mental Health Awareness Week

Plan events, workshops, and social media campaigns to promote emotional wellbeing. This initiative encourages open conversations about mental health and reduces stigma.

33. Host Career Talk Webinars

Invite professionals to discuss different career options and inspire fellow students. These webinars help students explore future career paths and gain real-world insights.

34. Set Up A School Recycling Program

Implement a recycling system and educate students about waste management. This project encourages environmental responsibility and helps reduce campus waste.

35. Organize A Local Park Beautification Project 

Plant flowers, paint benches, and clean up public spaces with friends and family. The project enhances community spaces and inspires civic pride.

36. Mentor Special Needs Students

Support learning and social inclusion by mentoring students with special educational needs. This experience builds empathy, patience, and leadership skills.

37. Volunteer With Habitat For Humanity

Get hands-on with house-building projects to help underprivileged families. It also teaches practical construction skills and teamwork.

38. Lead A Mindfulness & Meditation Group

Promote mental health through weekly guided meditation or mindfulness workshops. This activity encourages stress relief and emotional balance among students.

39. Host A Debate Or Public Speaking Workshop

Develop communication skills by leading debate clubs or competitions. This activity boosts confidence, critical thinking, and teamwork among participants.

40. Start A Peer Support Program

Train as a peer listener to help students who need someone to talk to confidentially. It promotes emotional well-being and creates a supportive school environment.

41. Plan A Book Donation Drive

Collect gently used books for local libraries, shelters, or schools. This initiative encourages literacy and gives underserved communities better access to reading materials.

42. Organize A Talent Show Fundraiser

Showcase your school’s hidden talents while raising money for a local cause. The event also fosters creativity and strengthens school community spirit.

43. Volunteer At Elderly Homes

Spend time with seniors through conversations, games, and performances. This project helps reduce loneliness among the elderly while building intergenerational friendships.

44. Teach Digital Skills To Seniors

Host workshops teaching elderly people how to use smartphones and the internet. It empowers seniors to stay connected with family and access online services independently.

45. Organize Inclusive Sports Events

Plan sports days for students of all abilities, promoting inclusivity. This fosters teamwork, breaks barriers, and celebrates diverse talents and abilities.

46. Start A Language Exchange Club

Help classmates practice new languages and explore different cultures through conversation. It encourages cultural understanding while enhancing speaking and listening skills.

47. Create A Local History Documentary

Research and film stories about your town’s history or cultural sites. This project enhances storytelling and technical skills while preserving local heritage for future generations.

48. Develop A “Zero-Waste” Challenge At School

Encourage students to reduce single-use plastic and monitor their daily waste. It promotes environmental awareness and helps students adopt sustainable habits in their daily lives.

49. Host Coding Or Graphic Design Workshops

Teach basic skills to classmates and help them build portfolios or projects. This project empowers peers to explore creative or tech-based careers through hands-on learning.

50. Initiate A Kindness Campaign

Launch a movement promoting random acts of kindness in school or online. It helps foster a supportive, inclusive environment and encourages empathy among students.

Related: The IB CAS Program: A Unique Approach to Learning

How To Choose The Right IB CAS Project For You?

Choosing the perfect CAS project can feel overwhelming, but it doesn’t have to be! Think of CAS as your personal playground, a chance to explore your interests, learn new skills, and give back to your community in meaningful ways. Follow these practical steps to choose a CAS project that truly excites you:

1. Reflect On Your Interests And Passions

Start by thinking deeply about what you enjoy doing or what excites your curiosity. Whether it’s sports, music, helping others, or exploring technology, choosing a project that connects with your interests will keep you motivated throughout your CAS experience. If you’ve always wanted to try something new, CAS is the perfect chance to step out of your comfort zone and explore.

2. Assess Your Strengths And Skills

Consider your existing strengths as well as the skills you’d like to develop. Are you good at organizing events, working creatively, or collaborating with others? Maybe you’d like to work on leadership, communication, or time management skills. Selecting a project that challenges you in the right way will help you grow both personally and academically.

3. Identify Community Needs

Look for gaps or issues in your school or local community that you feel passionate about addressing. Think about ways you can contribute meaningfully, whether by supporting environmental causes, helping younger students with their studies, or promoting mental health awareness. Projects that respond to real community needs tend to feel more purposeful and rewarding.

4. Blend Creativity, Activity, And Service

While it’s not required to cover all three CAS strands in a single project, choosing an activity that combines at least two of them can offer a richer experience. For example, planning a charity run could incorporate both activity and service, while organizing an art exhibition for charity blends creativity with service. This balance will help you develop as a well-rounded individual.

5. Set Achievable Goals

Clearly define what you want to accomplish with your CAS project. Setting realistic, measurable goals will help keep your project focused and manageable. Make sure your project fits alongside your IB coursework and other responsibilities, allowing you to commit consistently without feeling overwhelmed.

6. Think Long-Term Impact

Aim for a project that creates sustainable change or ongoing benefits, even after your direct involvement ends. Whether it’s starting a club, launching a community program, or building resources for future students, choosing a project with long-term potential can give your work a lasting legacy.

By choosing a CAS project that reflects your interests, builds your skills, serves your community, and aligns with your goals, you’ll not only fulfill the IB requirements but also gain a meaningful, enjoyable, and personally rewarding experience.

Related: List Of Top 10 Benefits Of The IB Diploma Programme

FAQs

1. What Counts As Creativity For CAS IB?

Creativity in CAS IB encompasses activities that involve the arts and other experiences that use creative thinking. This includes projects where students design, create, or perform, such as art, music, theater, and innovative problem-solving tasks.

2. What Is An Example Of An IB CAS Experience?

An example of an IB CAS experience is organizing and participating in a community clean-up event, where students engage in planning, teamwork, and service to improve their local environment.

3. Is It Possible To Fail CAS In IB?

Yes, it is possible to fail CAS in IB if a student does not meet the required learning outcomes, fail to adequately document their activities, or lack sustained commitment throughout the program. Completion of CAS is essential for earning the IB Diploma.

4. How To Get Creativity CAS Hours?

To get Creativity CAS hours, engage in activities that require creative thinking and expression, such as participating in a school play, creating artwork, learning a musical instrument, or organizing an art exhibit. Document your involvement and reflect on your experiences to earn the hours.

5. What Is A CAS Project For IB? 

A CAS Project is a collaborative, student-led experience that combines Creativity, Activity, and Service to address a need or interest. It helps students develop skills like teamwork, problem-solving, and leadership. Projects can range from organizing events to launching social initiatives.

6. What Does CAS Stand For In IB? 

CAS stands for Creativity, Activity, and Service. It is a core component of the IB Diploma Programme designed to encourage personal growth beyond academics. Students engage in experiences that foster emotional, physical, and social development.

7. What Are The 5 Stages Of A CAS Project? 

The five stages are Investigation, Preparation, Action, Reflection, and Demonstration. Students identify a need, plan their project, implement actions, reflect on their experience, and share outcomes. Following these stages ensures structured learning and meaningful impact.

8. Can A CAS Project Be Done Alone? 

Yes, a CAS project can be done individually, although collaboration is encouraged. Solo projects must still meet CAS requirements, including addressing a real need and showing personal growth. Whether individual or group, projects should follow the five CAS stages.

9. How Long Does A CAS Project Last? 

A CAS project must last at least one month from planning to completion. However, longer projects are encouraged if they provide sustained learning and impact. Duration depends on the project’s nature and goals.

10. What Are The 7 Learning Outcomes Of CAS? 

The seven outcomes are: identifying personal strengths, demonstrating growth and challenges, initiating and planning activities, showing commitment and perseverance, working collaboratively, engaging with global issues, and recognizing ethical choices and actions. Each outcome helps guide personal development. Students must achieve all outcomes at least once during their CAS experience.

Conclusion

IB CAS activities are an essential part of the International Baccalaureate program that provides students with the opportunity to develop their creativity, action, and service skills. These activities not only help students develop important life skills but also prepare them for future challenges.

Whether it’s taking up a new hobby, volunteering, or organizing a fundraising event, there are plenty of ways for IB students to get involved in their communities and make a positive impact.

If you are an IB student looking for support in your academic journey, Ignite Training Institute offers excellent resources and guidance to help you achieve your IBDP goals. With the right mindset, motivation, and support, you can turn your academic goals into a rewarding and enriching experience.
